title: A failed read of the saved cut seeds a fresh cut and saves it over the edits
body:
## Summary
useTrailerCut reads its own record with `loadStep`, which flattens a FAILED read and a NEVER-WRITTEN key into the same `undefined`. On a failed read of `script-trailer` with a readable picks record, the hook composes a fresh cut from the picks and its save effect writes it over the creator's edited cut. With both reads failed, the surface shows "no spine composed for this project yet" and tells the creator to go and pick beats. That is the wrong cause and the wrong remedy for a storage fault.

## Description
useTrailerCut.ts:59-61 reads both records with `loadStep`. stepStore.ts:563-566 documents the contract: "A FAILED read also lands here as the seeded default ... a caller that needs to tell the two apart calls `readStep` instead." The hook needs to tell them apart. A failed read routes to the seed branch at :75-84, and the save effect at :97-104 runs as soon as `hydrated` flips, so the composed cut overwrites the stored one. The sibling reader of this same record, useFrames.ts:186-195 and :250-255, already switched to `readStep` for exactly this reason. Its comment reads: "Taking the first branch on the second fact re-derived seeded frames over it and the debounced save below then wrote them to the key... the whole cut destroyed by a transient quota error nobody saw." FramesStep.tsx:108-133 is the render model: a Notice titled by trouble kind, the machine message verbatim, and a `reload` button. Step 2 is the writer of the record Step 3 protects, and it does not protect it.

## Flow
- The creator edits beat labels and text in Step 2, and the cut is saved under `script-trailer`.
- On a later visit the `script-trailer` read fails (blocked / transient) while the `research-beats` read succeeds.
- The hook sees `saved === undefined` and `confirmed` truthy, so it calls `composeCut(...)` and `setCut(composed)`.
- `hydrated` becomes true and `saveStep(projectId, "script-trailer", {cut: composed})` overwrites the edits.
- With both reads failed, TrailerScript.tsx:62-70 renders an info Notice telling the creator to go back to Step 1.

## Expected impact
Without this fix, a transient storage failure on Step 2 erases every beat edit on the next save. With it, the failure shows as a storage trouble with its real message, and nothing is written.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failed read of the saved cut must never be followed by a write over it, and must not render as "no spine"
Before: 2 `loadStep` reads in useTrailerCut.ts (:60, :61) and 0 `readStep`; the failed-read path composes and saves (seed branch :75-84 then the save at :100); TrailerScript has 0 trouble branches
After: 0 `loadStep` and 2 `readStep` in useTrailerCut.ts; a `loadTrouble` field on the api; the save effect is gated on `!loadTrouble`; TrailerScript renders a FramesStep-shaped error Notice (`kind` title, message verbatim, reload)
Method: probe - extend tests/golden-path/trailer-cut-lifecycle.probe.spec.ts (the existing dispatcher harness over fake-indexeddb)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/script/trailer/useTrailerCut.ts:59-61 (loadStep x2), :75-84 (seed on undefined), :97-104 (save effect); app/_phases/_shared/stepStore.ts:563-573 (loadStep flattens failure: 'a caller that needs to tell the two apart calls readStep'); app/_phases/frames/useFrames.ts:186-195,250-255 (the sibling reads the SAME script-trailer record with readStep and documents the destroy-by-transient-error); app/_phases/frames/FramesStep.tsx:108-133 (render model); app/_phases/script/trailer/TrailerScript.tsx:62-70 (failure renders as 'no spine' + 'Pick one beat per part in Step 1')
verify: Add a test to tests/golden-path/trailer-cut-lifecycle.probe.spec.ts named 'a FAILED read of a saved cut is trouble, never a seed'. Save an edited cut (label 'AN EDIT NOBODY MAY DISCARD') plus wholeSpinePicks(). Monkeypatch the fake-indexeddb object-store `get` so that the first request whose key contains 'script-trailer' fires onerror, then restore it in finally. drive() and settleUp(). Assert: api.cut === null, api.loadTrouble is truthy, and the record read back afterwards with readStep still has beats[0].label === 'AN EDIT NOBODY MAY DISCARD'. This is red on HEAD (the hook composes and saves over it) and green after. Also: `grep -c loadStep app/_phases/script/trailer/useTrailerCut.ts` drops from 3 to 0. Keep the existing 6 lifecycle tests green. Run npm test, npm run typecheck and npm run check:narration (the Notice body is the machine message, not new prose).

title: No-spine state is a 30-word essay with no way back to Step 1
body:
## Summary
The trailer Script step with no composed spine renders an info Notice. Its body is a sentence whose subject is the app ("The Script step opens on the spine Step 1 confirmed, it does not compose one..."), and it has no control at all, so the screen is a dead end. Its two sibling halves of the same step (ExplainerScript, MusicVideoScript) render `<UpstreamBreak>` with an "Open Research" action for the same situation. Frames, one step later, sends trailer creators here with a "Compose the cut" button.

## Description
TrailerScript.tsx:62-70 is the only upstream-blocked branch in ScriptStep that is still prose. ScriptStep.tsx:196-203 and :304-311 draw `<UpstreamBreak blockedAt="research" current="script" done={[]} action={{label:"Open Research", href:`/studio/${projectId}?step=research`}} />`. The signal README lists ScriptStep.tsx:237-242 as the essay UpstreamBreak replaced, and the trailer twin was missed. The cut-exists branch has a "<- step 1 · picks" link (:121-126), but the no-cut branch, the one that needs it most, has none. ShotSheet.tsx:147-153 shows the creator a "Compose the cut" action pointing at ?step=script, which lands on this dead end.

## Flow
- A trailer project with no confirmed spine. Frames shows UpstreamBreak with "Compose the cut", which goes to Script.
- Script (trailer) shows a cyan info box with two sentences and no button.
- The creator has to find Step 1 in the stepper themselves.

## Expected impact
This closes the loop Frames -> Script -> Research with one click on each hop, removes about 30 words of app narration, and makes the three halves of ScriptStep draw the same absence the same way.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an upstream-blocked step must draw the chain and offer the control that ends the block
Before: TrailerScript no-cut branch = 1 Notice, 2 sentences (31 words, subject 'The Script step'), 0 links/buttons; siblings in ScriptStep.tsx = 2 UpstreamBreak with action
After: TrailerScript no-cut branch = `<UpstreamBreak blockedAt="research" current="script" done={[]} action={{label:"Open Research", href:`/studio/${projectId}?step=research`}} />`, 0 prose sentences
Method: probe - source ratchet over the stripped TrailerScript.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/script/trailer/TrailerScript.tsx:62-70 (Notice + prose, no control); app/_phases/script/ScriptStep.tsx:196-203 and :304-311 (siblings use UpstreamBreak + 'Open Research'); app/_phases/frames/ShotSheet.tsx:147-153 ('Compose the cut' -> ?step=script lands here); components/ui/signal/README.md:151-160 (UpstreamBreak replaces exactly this essay shape); TrailerScript.tsx:121-126 (the step-1 link exists only when a cut exists)
verify: New probe tests/golden-path/trailer-no-spine-upstream.probe.spec.ts reads TrailerScript.tsx and passes it through stripComments (tests/golden-path/_helpers.ts). Assert: it contains '<UpstreamBreak', 'blockedAt="research"' and '?step=research'; it does not contain 'The Script step opens on'; UpstreamBreak is imported from '@/components/ui/signal'. Red on HEAD, green after. Keep the Notice import, because the stale-spine warning still uses it. Run npm run typecheck, npm run check:narration and npm test. Capture: node pipeline/cx-capture.mjs studio-script on a trailer project with no picks, and open the PNG to confirm the chain renders rather than a gap.

title: Rebuild keeps 'discarded' edits on screen and arms a dead promise picker
body:
## Summary
"rebuild from the new spine" says it discards your edits (TrailerScript.tsx:172-175), and the hook does replace the cut. But every editable child holds local state keyed by an id that survives the rebuild, so the screen keeps showing the old edits while the model holds the fixture text. A blur on any of those fields silently writes the "discarded" edit back. The promise ledger's beat picker can also point at a beat that no longer exists, and then "add" clears the sentence and adds nothing.

## Description
composeCut (cut.ts:49-68) takes beat ids from the slot VARIANT (trailerFixtures: `b-co-a`, `b-co-b`, ...). A rebuild that changes one pick leaves every other beat id unchanged. MovementSection keys BeatEditor on `b.id` (MovementSection.tsx:82), and BeatEditor seeds `useState(beat.label)` / `useState(beat.text)` once (BeatEditor.tsx:38-39) with no resync. So after a rebuild the inputs keep showing the edited label and text, while `beat.label` holds the fixture's. `flush` (:44-52) diffs local against `beat.label` on blur and on unmount and re-applies the edit. PromiseLedger seeds `beatId` once from `cut.beats[0]?.id` (PromiseLedger.tsx:26) and is never remounted, because TrailerScript renders it unkeyed (:224) and the cut id is constant (`cut-${projectId}`, cut.ts:59). If the selected beat was swapped out, `add()` calls `onAdd(staleId)`. `addPromise` goes through `mapBeat`, which returns the cut unchanged for an unknown id (cut.ts:77-79, :112-121), and `setSentence("")` then wipes what was typed. The payer and trade inputs use `defaultValue` (PromiseLedger.tsx:70, WithholdingPanel.tsx:68) and have the same shape of bug.

## Flow
- Edit beat 'cold open' text, then change one OTHER pick in Step 1 and come back.
- Click 'rebuild from the new spine'. The cold-open textarea still shows your edit (its id is unchanged), while the structure panel checks the fixture text.
- Tab through the textarea. The blur flushes the edit back into the cut, which the rebuild promised to discard.
- Earlier you had picked beat X in 'add a promise', and X was swapped out. Type a sentence and press add: the field clears and no row appears.

## Expected impact
After the fix, what the creator sees is what the checker reads and what gets saved. One destructive action keeps the promise it states, and one input stops eating typed text.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - after a rebuild, every visible field reflects the rebuilt cut, and 'add' either adds or is disabled
Before: 0 remount keys tied to a recompose; BeatEditor local state survives a rebuild for every unchanged slot (all slots but the changed one); PromiseLedger beatId is unvalidated against cut.beats (`disabled` checks only `!beatId`)
After: useTrailerCut exposes a `generation` counter bumped in `recompose`; TrailerScript keys the movement sections, PromiseLedger and WithholdingPanel on it; PromiseLedger resolves `beatId` against `cut.beats` (falls back to beats[0]) before add/disable
Method: probe - hook harness for the counter plus a source ratchet for the keys
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/script/trailer/useTrailerCut.ts:128-135 (recompose replaces cut; no generation); app/_phases/script/trailer/cut.ts:49-68 (beat ids = variant ids, stable across picks), :59 (constant cut id), :77-79 + :112-121 (unknown beatId -> unchanged cut); app/_phases/script/trailer/BeatEditor.tsx:38-39 (useState seeded once), :44-52 (flush re-applies on blur/unmount); app/_phases/script/trailer/MovementSection.tsx:82 (key=b.id); app/_phases/script/trailer/PromiseLedger.tsx:26 (beatId seeded once), :32-36 (add clears the sentence regardless), :115 (disabled only on !beatId); app/_phases/script/trailer/TrailerScript.tsx:172-175 ('discards your edits here'), :221-225 (children unkeyed)
verify: (1) In tests/golden-path/trailer-cut-lifecycle.probe.spec.ts, add 'recompose bumps the generation'. Save a cut composed from variant[0] picks and a research-beats record whose `confirmed` differs in one slot. settleUp, record api.generation, call api.recompose(), settleUp again, and assert generation increased by 1. Red on HEAD (undefined), green after. (2) Add a source ratchet in the same file or a new tests/golden-path/trailer-rebuild-remount.probe.spec.ts: stripped TrailerScript.tsx keys the sections wrapper, <PromiseLedger and <WithholdingPanel on api.generation; stripped PromiseLedger.tsx resolves the selection against cut.beats (e.g. contains 'cut.beats.some('). Land AFTER the 'failed read' finding: both touch useTrailerCut.ts and TrailerScript.tsx. Run npm test and npm run typecheck.

title: Energy-curve labels are SVG text at fontSize 9: under the 16px floor
body:
## Summary
EnergyCurve draws its movement labels as SVG `<text fontSize={9}>` inside a `viewBox="0 0 640 140"` that scales to the figure. Rendered size is 9 x (svg width / 640) px: 5.9px at the component's own `min-w-[420px]`, and at least the 16px `text-label` floor only once the svg is 1138px or wider. On top of that it is painted at fillOpacity 0.45. It is the only SVG `<text>` with a font size in app/ and components/, and `npm run check:type` cannot see it.

## Description
The house rule is "Nothing below text-label (1rem). npm run check:type fails the build otherwise" (signal README:243-245; globals.css:38). check-type-scale.mjs matches only `text-xs`, `text-[Npx]` and inline-style `fontSize: "Npx"` / `"Nrem"`. A JSX attribute `fontSize={9}` in user units passes. The movement labels are not decoration: they are the only names on the curve ("rung 2", "reset"), and the aria-label lists only y-values. The fix keeps the SVG for the line and dots, and moves the labels into an HTML row under it: absolutely positioned spans at `left: ${x*100}%` with `font-jetbrains text-label text-white/45` and `-translate-x-1/2`. The labels then live on the real type scale and stay legible at every width.

## Flow
- Open Script on a trailer project at a laptop width. The labels under the energy curve read at roughly 9-13px, faded to 45%.

## Expected impact
The curve's only labels become readable at every width. This also removes the one type-floor escape in the tree.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every rendered label is at least text-label (16px) at every container width
Before: 1 `<text ... fontSize={9}>` (EnergyCurve.tsx:84-95); rendered px = 9*w/640, i.e. 5.9px at w=420, 11.3px at w=800, below 16px for any w < 1138
After: 0 `<text` and 0 `fontSize=` in EnergyCurve.tsx; labels are HTML spans carrying `text-label`
Method: probe - source ratchet over the stripped EnergyCurve.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/script/trailer/EnergyCurve.tsx:19 (W=640), :54-57 (viewBox + w-full min-w-[420px]), :84-95 (<text fontSize={9} fillOpacity={0.45}>); grep -rn 'fontSize={' app components --include=*.tsx -> 1 hit (this file); pipeline/check-type-scale.mjs:44-47 (regexes see class + style-object sizes only); components/ui/signal/README.md:243-245
verify: New probe tests/golden-path/energy-curve-type-floor.probe.spec.ts. Run stripComments on EnergyCurve.tsx and assert it does not match /<text[\s>]/ or /fontSize=/, and that it contains 'text-label'. Red on HEAD, green after. Keep the svg's role=img and aria-label. Then capture studio-script for a trailer at --width 1280 with pipeline/cx-capture.mjs and open the PNG: the labels must sit under their beats and not overlap. Widening check-type-scale.mjs to catch SVG fontSize is a pipeline/ change and out of this context (Lane B follow-on).

title: CheckList greys 'unmeasured' with the glyph its siblings use for n/a
body:
## Summary
Meters.tsx's CheckList draws an `unmeasured` craft check as a grey "—" at white/35 labelled "not measured". GatePanel, which sits beside it, and StructurePanel both draw unmeasured as an amber "?" and use "—" for not-engaged / n/a. So the same glyph means two different verdicts on one page. GatePanel's header names the greyed-out version as the lie this app refuses: "A gate that greys out what it could not test is telling the same lie the ledger told, in a nicer font." The same verdict also has three names: "not checked" (GatePanel), "unmeasured" (StructurePanel) and "not measured" (CheckList).

## Description
Meters.tsx:70-75 `CHECK.unmeasured = { mark: "—", cls: "text-white/35", label: "not measured" }`. GatePanel.tsx:25-31 has `unmeasured: { glyph: "?", cls: "text-amber-300", label: "not checked" }` and `"not-engaged": { glyph: "—", cls: "text-white/25", label: "n/a" }`. StructurePanel.tsx:33-38 follows GatePanel's glyphs. The rows are reachable: renders.ts:58 and :103 ship `state: "unmeasured"` checks ('causal-opener density'), and CheckList renders them in HypothesisColumn.tsx:143. Contrast of white/35 on --gt-ink #080a10 is 3.14:1. Fix: `unmeasured: { mark: "?", cls: "text-amber-300", label: "not checked" }`, which matches GatePanel's glyph, tone and words. The sr-only label then says the same thing GatePanel's label says.

## Flow
- Script (explainer) -> the hypothesis column shows the craft checklist: '— causal-opener density — not counted on this render'.
- In the gate panel next to it, '—' means n/a, and an untested rule is an amber '?'.

## Expected impact
One glyph keeps one meaning across the three checkers on Step 2, and the honest-failure rule holds in the last place it was greyed out.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an unmeasured check is drawn as loudly as the gate draws it, with the same glyph and words
Before: CheckList unmeasured = '—', white/35 (3.14:1), 'not measured'; 3 names for one verdict across GatePanel / StructurePanel / CheckList; '—' = n/a in 2 of 3
After: CheckList unmeasured = '?', text-amber-300, 'not checked'; '—' means n/a everywhere it appears
Method: probe - source ratchet over the stripped Meters.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/script/_parts/Meters.tsx:70-75 (unmeasured '—' white/35 'not measured'); app/_phases/script/_parts/GatePanel.tsx:11-16 ('unmeasured is rendered as loudly as violation... greys out... the same lie'), :25-31 (unmeasured '?' amber 'not checked'; not-engaged '—' 'n/a'); app/_phases/script/trailer/StructurePanel.tsx:33-38 (same glyphs as GatePanel); app/_phases/script/renders.ts:58,:103 (reachable unmeasured rows); app/_phases/script/_parts/HypothesisColumn.tsx:143 (consumer); contrast white/35 on #080a10 = 3.14:1 (computed)
verify: New probe tests/golden-path/checklist-unmeasured-loud.probe.spec.ts runs stripComments on Meters.tsx and extracts the `unmeasured:` entry of CHECK. Assert it contains 'mark: "?"', 'text-amber-300' and 'label: "not checked"', and that it does not contain the em-dash glyph. Red on HEAD, green after. Confirm that `grep -rn "not measured" tests` has no assertion on this copy (it has none today). HypothesisColumn.tsx:133's own sr-only 'not measured' is a separate surface and out of this context. Run npm test, npm run typecheck and npm run check:type.

lens_checked.visual-craft: Read in full TrailerScript, BeatEditor, StructurePanel, EnergyCurve, MovementSection, PromiseLedger, RaisesChips, WithholdingPanel, ConnectorPick and _parts/Meters, plus signal/README, UpstreamBreak and the Ghost/Tally/Hint call sites. Checked tokens and chip spellings against signal (all used correctly), the type floor (EnergyCurve fontSize=9 was the only escape; finding filed), and alpha on #080a10. StructurePanel cites at text-white/25 = 2.14:1 is noted but not filed: it is 59 sites repo-wide, a systemic token call rather than this context's.
lens_checked.ux-reviewer: Traced useTrailerCut hydrate/seed/save/recompose against every child's local state (BeatEditor useState, PromiseLedger beatId, defaultValue inputs); the no-spine dead end vs the ScriptStep siblings and ShotSheet's 'Compose the cut' hop. Rebuild has no confirm: not filed separately, because the consequence row (discards your edits) is drawn before the click and the real defect is that it does not discard what it shows.
lens_checked.state-coverage: useTrailerCut sources (script-trailer and research-beats reads): zero rows leads to the info Notice, failure leads to the SAME Notice or a seed-and-overwrite (finding filed), never-returns leads to the 'opening the project's cut...' line (same spelling as 4 research surfaces; not filed). The staleSpine true/false/null and spineReopened branches each render distinctly. PromiseLedger and MovementSection empty states use Ghost.
lens_checked.copy-auditor: Checked the Hint bodies at TrailerScript:139,148,202,213 and EnergyCurve:50 (all 14 words or fewer; within budget); StructurePanel against GatePanel names (filed as the CheckList pair); 'picked parts' vs beats.length (equal by construction: one beat per slot).
lens_checked.accessibility-checker: aria-pressed on the RaisesChips and ConnectorPick toggles; role=group names; BeatEditor aria-labels; Segmented in WithholdingPanel; sr-only on the spine chips; EnergyCurve role=img. The promise-add sentence input names itself by placeholder only: weak, but accepted by accname. Not filed.

lens_no_surface.mobile-specialist: desktop editor surface; EnergyCurve has min-w-[420px] with overflow-x-auto by design
